deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page, so there is nothing to reconstruct. Folio 59v is not a Riemann manuscript leaf. It is page 6 of a printed German university lecture catalogue (Vorlesungsverzeichnis), almost certainly that of the Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Berlin. The evidence: the lecturers named (Trendelenburg, Michelet, Gabler, Werder, Beneke, v. Henning, Steiner, Ohm) and, on the adjacent pages, Lejeune-Dirichlet, Encke, Dove, Magnus, Mitscherlich, H. Rose, Joachimsthal, Dirksen and Grüson; the Charité; Ziegelstraße.

The page continues the section 'Philosophische Wissenschaften', which lists logic, metaphysics, psychology, practical philosophy, natural law, philosophy of religion, history of philosophy and conversatoria. It then opens 'Mathematische Wissenschaften'.

The mathematical entries on this page are:
- Steiner: geometric exercises, Wednesdays 9-10, public.
- Steiner: the properties of maxima and minima of figures in the plane, on the sphere and in space, developed synthetically (his isoperimetric work), Tuesdays and Thursdays 9-11, private.
- Martin Ohm: algebra and analysis of the finite, following part 2 of his 'System der Mathematik', 2nd edition.
- Ohm: the theory of higher equations; the entry begins here and continues on page 7.

The following page lists Dirichlet's number theory and his 'Anwendung der Integralrechnung auf die Zahlenlehre', and Joachimsthal's integral calculus. The page carries no handwritten annotations.

The catalogue was printed after 1841, since the previous page cites Kranichfeld's 1841 book. The mix of lecturers fits the period when Riemann was a student in Berlin, 1847-1849; the semester is my inference and is not stated on the page. Its presence in the Riemann Nachlass is presumably because Riemann kept the catalogue of the semester(s) he attended. He is known to have heard Dirichlet (number theory, definite integrals), Steiner, Jacobi and Eisenstein in Berlin. The page is a biographical/contextual document, not a mathematical one.

results.what: Printed listing of Berlin university lectures in philosophy and mathematics (Steiner on synthetic maxima/minima of figures, Ohm on algebra and higher equations); context for Riemann's Berlin student years
results.modern_name: University lecture catalogue (Vorlesungsverzeichnis), not a mathematical result

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed university lecture catalogue with no handwriting or mathematics by Riemann. Its only interest is biographical: it documents the courses on offer, probably during his Berlin semesters 1847-49, which is already well known.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially accurate.
'Abrifs' and 'läfst' render the long-s/ß ligature of the print; read them as 'Abriß' and 'läßt'.
'entwikkelt' reflects the period hyphenation 'entwik-kelt' and is correct for the print.
'Mi-chelet' and 'Stei-ner' are line-break hyphenations, correctly joined in the transcription.
In the Ohm entry the closing quotation mark after 'Systems der Mathematik' appears in the print as ',,Systems der Mathematik,"'; this does not affect the content.
